newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus seeks arrest of Turks for August killing.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus seeks arrest of Turks for August killing.

text.p: Cyprus has issued arrest warrants for six men from the Turkish north suspected of beating to death a Greek Cypriot youth during clashes along the ceasefire line that divides the island, its attorney-general said on Friday.
Among those wanted is Mehmet Mustafa Aslan, leader of the Turkish Islamist Grey Wolves movement in Turkish-held Cyprus, Attorney-General Alecos Markides told a news conference.

Cypriot authorities say all six - two Turkish Cypriots and four Turks who settled in the north from the Turkish mainland - had been identified as being party to the killing of Greek Cypriot Tasos Isaac, 24.

"Inquiries were headed by the central intelligence service and it managed to identify people shown in photographs or films who, according to other sources of information we have, were party to the murder," said Markides.

Isaac was clubbed to death by a group of people from the Turkish-occupied areas on August 11 during demonstrations along the United-Nations controlled buffer zone. Cypriot authorities said most were members of the Grey Wolves movement.

Isaac was participating in a rally organised by a local motorcyclists group to protest against the island's division by Turkey, which occupied Cyprus's northern third in 1974 in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling Greece.

Three days after Isaac's death and hours after his funeral his cousin, Solomos Solomos, 26, was shot dead by Turkish forces in the same area when he attempted to climb a flagpole to remove the Turkish flag a few metres inside Turkish-held territory.
Cypriot authorities have issued arrest warrants against five Turks in connection with Solomos' killing, including the former commander of Turkish forces in Cyprus, Hasan Kundaci.
"We have conveyed the warrants (over Solomos' death) to Interpol and in case they travel to any country we have an extradition treaty with we will seek their extradition," Markides said.
